result.title: After the Federation: Benchmarking Knowledge Portability to Heterogeneous Newcomers
result.summary: Once historical clients become unavailable, a federation must serve newcomers through the artifact it leaves behind. How much of its knowledge remains useful in an architecture chosen afterward? We introduce FEDNBO, a seven-dataset benchmark that separates knowledge supply, policy identification, and private-model compilation under disjoint data roles. Controlled studies expose inflated oracle gains, architecture-dependent transfer reversals, and a gap between teacher accuracy and private-model utility. Ordinary public-response distillation provides a competitive reference without public task labels or newcomer samples: gains over strengthened local training are 23.52 and 16.62 percentage points on 300 CelebA identities and 300 FedEMNIST writers, respectively. In a complete-pipeline FedEMNIST comparison, this reference reaches 97.13% accuracy with 12.4 seconds of compilation per architecture, versus 97.03% and 67.5 seconds for a HeteroFedTTA reconstruction at the same epoch budget. Equal-count public-input interventions extend support sensitivity to trainable visual backbones. Together, these results establish an auditable benchmark and a strong reference for evaluating the utility, cost and reliability of post-federation knowledge transfer.

AI.relevance_reason: 该工作是联邦学习跨架构知识迁移与私有模型编译的基准与蒸馏对比，虽涉及「公共响应蒸馏」等训练监督线索，但研究对象是异构新客户端上的模型可移植性与成本，未触及视觉 latent 状态的生成、使用或停止决策，与 LVR 主线缺少可核查的具体联系。
